fixtures.facts:
Repository plan-marshall (Python 3, stdlib scripts run by agents through an executor). Plan ids and paths are passed as command-line arguments by a model and are untrusted. get_store_dir('plans', plan_id) joins the plan id under the plans store; the module file_ops also offers is_valid_plan_id(). Plan directories are siblings named by plan id (for example .plan/local/plans/fix-1 and .plan/local/plans/fix-10).

Change (unified diff):
diff --git a/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/manage-files/scripts/_artifact_paths.py b/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/manage-files/scripts/_artifact_paths.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/manage-files/scripts/_artifact_paths.py
@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+"""Resolve caller-supplied artifact paths inside a plan directory and write artifacts there."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from file_ops import get_store_dir  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+
+
+def resolve_artifact_path(plan_id: str, relative: str) -> Path:
+    """Resolve ``relative`` inside the plan's ``artifacts/`` directory.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: when the resolved path would leave the plan directory.
+    """
+    plan_dir = get_store_dir('plans', plan_id)
+    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(plan_dir / 'artifacts', relative))
+    if not candidate.startswith(str(plan_dir)):
+        raise ValueError(f'artifact path escapes the plan directory: {relative!r}')
+    return Path(candidate)
+
+
+def cmd_write_artifact(plan_id: str, relative: str, content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Handler of ``manage-files write-artifact --plan-id P --path R --content C``."""
+    try:
+        path = resolve_artifact_path(plan_id, relative)
+    except ValueError as refused:
+        return {'status': 'error', 'error': 'path_outside_plan', 'message': str(refused)}
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(content, encoding='utf-8')
+    return {'status': 'success', 'path': str(path)}

seeded_defects.description: The request_uri from the network response is appended to the redirect URL unencoded: a value carrying "&" or "#" injects or truncates parameters of the front-channel redirect.
The exception message embeds the whole authorization URL (state, nonce, PKCE challenge) and chains the decoder exception that echoes the offending pair; it reaches logs and possibly responses.
Duplicate parameters are no longer refused; the last occurrence wins, so a smuggled second redirect_uri or scope overrides the first in the pushed request.

diff --git a/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/workflow-integration-git/scripts/_branch_cleanup.py b/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/workflow-integration-git/scripts/_branch_cleanup.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/marketplace/bundles/plan-marshall/skills/workflow-integration-git/scripts/_branch_cleanup.py
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+"""Remote branch deletion for branch cleanup after a merged pull request."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+# A branch name as git check-ref-format accepts it, restricted further: it starts with an
+# alphanumeric (so it can never be read as an option) and carries no range or lock suffix.
+_BRANCH_NAME = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}')
+
+
+def is_deletable_branch_name(branch: str) -> bool:
+    """True when ``branch`` is a plain branch name this module may pass to git."""
+    return (
+        _BRANCH_NAME.fullmatch(branch) is not None
+        and '..' not in branch
+        and '//' not in branch
+        and not branch.endswith(('/', '.', '.lock'))
+    )
+
+
+def delete_remote_branch(worktree: Path, branch: str, timeout_seconds: int = 60) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Delete ``branch`` on ``origin``; the result is a status dict, never an exception."""
+    if not is_deletable_branch_name(branch):
+        return {'status': 'error', 'error': 'invalid_branch_name'}
+    command = ['git', '-C', str(worktree), 'push', 'origin', '--delete', f'refs/heads/{branch}']
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_seconds, check=False)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        return {'status': 'error', 'error': 'timeout', 'timeout_seconds': timeout_seconds}
+    if result.returncode != 0:
+        return {'status': 'error', 'error': 'push_failed', 'exit_code': result.returncode}
+    return {'status': 'success', 'branch': branch}
